$comment: The React half of target selection. rust-output-v1 amendment 006 and typescript-output-v1 amendment 002 admit react as the fourth value of the target enum and hand every target react request and every som.dsl-bundle.v2 bundle with target react to this contract. Requests without target, or with target python, rust or typescript, are not covered here and keep their responses, except for the invalid-target texts those amendments change. Diagnostics, transport limits and the error envelope are unchanged from som.compiler-api.v1.

x-target-selection.react: A som.dsl-bundle.v2 bundle with target react, or one diagnostic.
x-target-selection.others: absent, python, rust and typescript: rust-output-v1 and typescript-output-v1 x-target-selection, unchanged by this contract.

invalid.span: the raw value token of the target member
invalid.cause: Target must be the string python, rust, typescript or react.
invalid.allowed_form: Omit target, or use target python, rust, typescript or react.
invalid.rule: rust-output-v1 amendment 006 and typescript-output-v1 amendment 002 adopt these two texts for every target value outside the enum, in place of the three-target texts.

x-target-selection.cli: som compile --target react forwards the string as the target member without checking it. A server refusal exits with status 2.
x-target-selection.before_phase_1: Until a build implements react-output-v1 phase 1, target react gets the three-target INVALID_SCHEMA refusal of rust-output-v1. No candidate is prepared from such a build.

UNSUPPORTED_TARGET.use: The code rust-output-v1 introduced. For target react: a prompt that passes existing validation but is outside React output phase 1, or a React bundle whose prompt is outside phase 1. Causes and allowed forms are the scope.json refusals of this contract.

x-check-order: transport limit and JSON parse, including duplicate members
CNL parse or prompt JSON schema
existing compiler-v1 semantic validation, unchanged (this already refuses a v3 filter field named limit or offset, compiler-v1 amendment 003)
React profile, only when target is react, in the scope.json refusal_order (UNSUPPORTED_TARGET)
planning, with SCOPE_TOO_LARGE for a React DSL over 19 files or over 64 blocks in total, or an assemble envelope over 2097152 bytes
x-assemble-check-order: transport limit, JSON parse and envelope schema
bundle version dispatch: only a bundle whose version member is the string som.dsl-bundle.v2 continues; every other bundle keeps the compiler-v1 order and result unchanged

target dispatch: a bundle whose target member is the string react continues below; target rust follows rust-output-v1 and target typescript follows typescript-output-v1; any other value is INVALID_SCHEMA at /bundle/target after the members and version checks of the rust-output-v1 check_schema order
bundle schema som.dsl-bundle.v2.react in the rust-output-v1 check_schema order, and at most 64 blocks in total (INVALID_SCHEMA at the failing pointer)
hashes: prompt_sha256, dsl_sha256, then payload_sha256 = H({version,target,prompt,dsl,assets}) (BUNDLE_HASH_MISMATCH)
asset descriptors equal the active React manifest (ASSET_HASH_MISMATCH at /bundle/assets)
React profile (UNSUPPORTED_TARGET at /bundle/prompt plus the scope.json pointer)

catalog and composition: the DSL equals the frozen plan for the prompt. Files are compared in order: a file path that differs is INVALID_COMPOSITION at /bundle/dsl/files/<i>/path; then the blocks in order, and a block whose id, name, params or refs differ, or a block the plan does not have, is INVALID_COMPOSITION at /bundle/dsl/files/<i>/blocks/<j>/id; a file the plan has and the DSL lacks is INVALID_COMPOSITION at /bundle/dsl/files. Every block id is an admitted react. block of the catalog.
render and output checks: the 19 product-layout.json files, the fixed files equal to the reference bytes

x-manifest.shared_with_rust: grammar, compiler_contract, selection_policy, literal_policy, serializer and semantic_contracts equal the Rust manifest's descriptors for the same build.
x-manifest.target_contract: id som.react-output-contract.v1; sha256 is the canonical hash of the sealed receipt's files map, as for rust-output-v1.
x-manifest.catalog: id som.react-catalog.v1; descriptor {id, sha256} with the SHA-256 of the bytes of catalog/react-catalog.v1.json as embedded in som-targets.
x-manifest.block_library: id som.react-block-library.v1; descriptor {id, sha256} with the SHA-256 of the concatenated text of the React renderer sources that hold the block bodies and the fixed reference files, in the order som-targets/src/react/mod.rs lists them, as the Rust BLOCK_LIBRARY_TEXT.
x-manifest.backend: id som.react-backend.v1; sha256 = H({"version": "som.react-backend.v1", "files": {path: SHA-256 of the file text}}), the formula of the Rust backend descriptor. The files map has every source that decides the React bundle and its files, keyed by som-rs-relative path: every file under som-targets/src/react/, plus the shared som-targets/Cargo.toml, src/lib.rs, src/main.rs and src/profile.rs. Shared files appear in every backend map, so an edit to one changes the Rust, TypeScript and React descriptors: it needs an amendment of each contract and is recorded as a bundle compatibility break for each target.
x-manifest.formatter: toolchain.json formatter id and sha256. The formatter does not run at compile or assemble; the descriptor pins the prettier that format_check uses.
